propositions: The undecomposed hard-override axis fires on 0.107% of plan-v3 verified findings (11/10,250) and 0.153% of plan-v4 (18/11,773), two orders of magnitude below other severity axes, yet floors impact to 0.85 with unconditional force.

The stated justification—that G5 deterministic suppression prevents false flat-plan findings on ticketed children—is contradicted: the G5 veto fired zero times across 2,000 reviews, and 90%+ of reviewed tickets are childless (inapplicable population).

In 25 of 29 fires, the undecomposed axis alone was the hard override present; 16 fires graded low yet still blocked on the 0.85 floor, indicating miscalibrated grade-to-floor mapping identical to pre-retune miscalibrations in ac_unverifiable and divergent_implementation axes.

The inverse population (33 plan-v3 and 17 plan-v4 findings text-matching the undecomposed regex but scored none) is regex false positives on code/module decomposition, not missed flat-plan defects; no large dark class analogous to the divergence recall problem exists.

The axis is not inert or unreachable, but its grades are not gated on severity: all non-none grades floor equally, violating the principle that low severity should not produce blocks without additional criteria.
